questions.question: From metric:web:error_rate:30 and metric:cart:error_rate:30, show the error_rate series for minutes 20‑35 to see the spike pattern.
For log:web.upstream_502 (evidence log:web.upstream_502) and log:cart.npe, give sample logs around minute 30 to identify root cause.
Regarding deploy:d6 (cart) at minute 30, were there any related config or flag changes that could affect price calculation?

findings.text: web error_rate (baseline ≈ 0.002) stays low (0.0015‑0.0024) until minute 30, then spikes to 0.215 and remains high (0.201) at minute 33.
cart error_rate (baseline ≈ 0.003) is stable (0.0026‑0.0036) before minute 30, jumps to 0.2269 at minute 30 and climbs to 0.2559 by minute 33.
Cart v2.14.0 'price calculator refactor' deployed at minute 30, coinciding with fault onset.
Cart throws NullPointerException in PriceCalculator.apply (build 2.14.0), 5160 occurrences since minute 30.
Web receives 502s from cart on POST /cart/items, 6003 occurrences since minute 30, causing SLO breach.
Cart error rate spiked 80x (0.003 to 0.241) and latency p50 rose 67% at minute 30.
Web error rate spiked 90x (0.002 to 0.181) at minute 30 due to upstream cart failures.
No config or flag changes were made around deploy:d6; all flags remained at their default values, so the price calculation issue stems from the code change itself.

hypotheses.summary: The price calculator refactor deployed at minute 30 (v2.14.0) introduced a NullPointerException, causing cart errors and upstream 502s that breached the SLO.

data.rationale: Rolling back cart to the previous stable version removes the faulty price calculator code that caused the NPE and upstream 502 errors.

prose.summary: A bad deployment of the cart service (seq 32) caused a rapid increase in error rate, triggering an alert (seq 35). Investigation quickly identified the cart deployment as the source, a rollback to version 2.13.4 was proposed, approved, and applied (seq 58‑60), restoring service and meeting the SLO within 5 minutes (seq 67).
prose.rootCause: Fault injected: a bad_deploy of the cart component introduced at minute 30 (seq 32) caused the outage.
prose.whatWentWell: Alert fired promptly, investigation began within minutes, hypothesis ranking correctly pinpointed the cart deployment, the rollback proposal was approved quickly, remediation was applied without delay, and the SLO recovered in 5 healthy minutes.
actionItems: Add automated pre‑deployment health checks for the cart service.
Introduce canary releases with monitoring to catch bad_deploy early.
Automate rollback to the last known good version upon similar alerts.
Review and fine‑tune alert thresholds for faster detection.
